source_of_truth: Read by hand in app/components/auth/LoginForm.vue: the password <input id="password"> (line 10) has no <label for="password"> anywhere, is not wrapped in a <label>, and carries no aria-label / aria-labelledby / title. A screen-reader user reaches an unnamed edit field. The username <input> above it is correctly labelled by a <label for="username"> + matching id, so it is NOT a defect. Separately, the <form> (line 7) has a submit handler but no pending/loading flag in the script and no disabled/loading binding on its submit button, which a correct auditor flags at heuristic level. Derived from the markup, not from the tool.

expected.rationale: the password input has no associated label by any mechanism (for/id, wrapping label, aria-label, aria-labelledby, title); the semantic engine knows the full element tree, so the absence is proven and the correct level is confirmed.

the form has a @submit handler but no pending/loading identifier in <script setup> and no disabled/loading/aria-busy binding on the submit button; a re-entrant submit is possible. Static analysis cannot prove a guard is truly absent at runtime, so heuristic is the honest level.

forbidden.why_not_a_defect: the username input (line 9) is correctly labelled by <label for="username"> with a matching id; flagging it would be a false positive
